description: A festival producer must finalize the merchandise settlement plan for the closing artist's one-night show, including the artist's share, inventory allocation, point-of-sale quantity, tax treatment, and payout timing.

shared_context.S1: The closing artist will sell merchandise at the festival's official store after the artist's one-night performance.
shared_context.S2: The festival and the artist have agreed to use the festival's point-of-sale system and settle the artist's share after the event.
shared_context.S3: Maya has authority to approve the final merchandise settlement plan.
shared_context.S4: At the daily production closeout, Maya routinely reviews the merchandise, finance, and artist-liaison plans with the responsible leads before approving the event paperwork.

PF1.text: Jonah reviewed the signed artist merchandise rider this morning: the artist receives 75 percent of net merchandise receipts, and 120 units of the artist's numbered poster must be held back for the artist before general sales begin; Jonah has not yet attached the rider to the settlement worksheet.

PF2.text: Tessa tested the festival's point-of-sale inventory configuration yesterday and confirmed that it can process at most 420 artist merchandise units during this event; she recorded the result in the store log but has not updated Maya's draft plan.

PF3.text: Luis confirmed the event's applicable city tax rate with the festival's tax preparer this afternoon: merchandise sales require 8.25 percent tax, and the artist payout must be released by 10:00 AM the next day; he has not entered those figures into the finance schedule.

acceptance_conditions: The artist must receive exactly 75 percent of net merchandise receipts.
Exactly 120 units must be reserved for the artist before general sales.
Exactly 420 units may be offered through the point-of-sale system.
The merchandise settlement must apply exactly 8.25 percent city tax.
The artist payout deadline must be 10:00 AM the next day.
A merchandise-rider commitment must be logged.
A point-of-sale-capacity commitment must be logged.
A tax-and-payout commitment must be logged.

decisive_facts.why: The signed rider changes the artist share to exactly 75 percent, requires exactly 120 units to be reserved, and creates the merchandise-rider commitment.
The tested point-of-sale limit changes the quantity offered for sale to exactly 420 units and requires the point-of-sale-capacity commitment.
The tax-preparer confirmation changes the tax rate to exactly 8.25 percent, sets the payout deadline to 10:00 AM the next day, and requires the tax-and-payout commitment.
